decision: What visual structure should the 'How we're different' comparison use?
primary_axis: comparison structure: our-answer-first list vs plan-style cards vs one-at-a-time head to head
invariants: approved copy (PR #22): heading, 3 alternatives, 5 rows, all cell text
warm-look tokens (Geist, mono labels, grey cards, grainy wash, orange square)

options.bet: Lead every row with our answer in large type; the three alternatives sit beside it as small grey context
options.benefit: Reads as a list of promises; no table chrome; phones need no special layout
options.cost: Alternatives are quieter, so the contrast is less visual
options.risk: Can read as a feature list rather than a comparison

options.bet: Four cards like the pricing plans; ours is the featured card with the wash, lifted
options.benefit: Familiar pattern that matches Pricing right below it; strong 'pick us' signal
options.cost: Each row is read across four cards, harder to compare row by row
options.risk: Phones swipe sideways, so most parents see only our card and one other

options.bet: One alternative at a time against us, chosen with a toggle
options.benefit: Two columns fit every screen; the parent picks the option they already use
options.cost: Hides the full picture; needs a tap
options.risk: Parents who do not tap see only learning centres
